                                     PUBLIC HEARING(S)

REZ2023-000816 – The Magna Metro Township Council has initiated a public process to explore
rezoning property located on Magna Main Street (2700 South), located between 8800 West and
9200 West from the existing C-3 (Commercial) and R-2-6.5 (Medium Density Residential) to the
Downtown Historic District (DH) Mixed Use Zone. Acres: 22.5. Location: Magna Main Street,
between 8800 West and 9200 West, 9180 West between 2600 South and 2700 South, and 8950
West, between 2600 South and 2700 South (See attached map). Planner: Brian Tucker
(Motion/Voting)

The Planning Commission will hold a public hearing to take public comment and discuss rezoning
property to the Downtown Historic District (DH) Mixed Use Zone, a zone that was adopted in July
2022 to implement the vision identified in the Magna General Plan (2021) for the Historic
Preservation Future Land Use Area. The Downtown Historical Mixed-Use Zone is intended to
promote a mixture of uses consistent with the district’s historic role in Magna. Emphasis is placed
on entertainment, theaters, restaurants, retail, and specialty shops. Medium-density residential and
office infill on upper floors is encouraged, as is the continued presence of the library, museum,
senior center, and supporting uses. After taking public comment, the Planning Commission will
make a recommendation to the Magna Metro Township Council. The Council will then hold a
public meeting, at a later date, where they may take action that includes rezoning some or all of
the property identified in this notice.

             Rules of Conduct for Planning Commission Meetings
PROCEDURE FOR PUBLIC COMMENT

1.   Any person or entity may appear in person or be represented by an authorized agent at any meeting of the
     Commission.

2.   Unless altered by the Chair, the order of the procedure on an application shall be:

     a. The supporting agency staff will introduce the application, including staff’s recommendations and a
        summary of pertinent written comments and reports concerning the application

     b. The applicant will be allowed up to 15 minutes to make their presentation.

     c. The Community Council representative can present their comments as applicable.

     d. Where applicable, persons in favor of, or not opposed to, the application will be invited to speak.

     e. Where applicable, persons opposing the application, in whole or in part will be invited to speak.

     f. Where applicable, the applicant will be allowed 5 minutes to provide concluding statements.

     g. Surrebuttals may be allowed at the discretion of the Chair.

CONDUCT FOR APPLICANTS AND THE PUBLIC

1.   Speakers will be called to the podium by the Chair.

2.   Each speaker, before talking, shall give his or her name and address.

3.   All comments should be directed to the Commissioners, not to the staff or to members of the audience.

4.   For items where there are several people wishing to speak, the Chair may impose a time limit, usually 3
     minutes per person, or 5 minutes for a group spokesperson. If a time limit is imposed on any member or
     spokesperson of the public, then the same time limit is imposed on other members or spokespersons of the
     public, respectively.

5.   Unless otherwise allowed by the Chair, no questions shall be asked by the speaker or Commission Members.

6.   Only one speaker is permitted before the Commission at a time.

7.   The discussion must be confined to essential points stated in the application bearing on the desirability or
     undesirability of the application.

8.   The Chair may cease any presentation or information that has already been presented and acknowledge that it
     has been noted in the public record.

9.   No personal attacks shall be indulged in by either side, and such action shall be sufficient cause for stopping the
     speaker from proceeding.

10. No applause or public outbursts shall be permitted.

11. The Chair or supporting agency staff may request police support to remove offending individuals who refuse to
    abide by these rules.

12. After the public comment portion of a meeting or hearing has concluded, the discussion will be limited to the
    Planning Commission and Staff.

                                           Files # CUP2023-000792

                                     Conditional Use Summary

Public Body: Magna Planning Commission
Meeting Date: March 9, 2023
Parcel ID: 14-30-456-014-0000
Current Zone: R-1-6
Property Address: 8997 S New House Drive
Request: Conditional Use for a home daycare
Applicant Name: Zhandra Luzardo
MSD Planner: Justin Smith
MSD Planning Staff Recommendation: Planning Commission Approval


PROJECT SUMMARY

The applicant, Zhandra Luzardo, is applying for a conditional use for a home day care for up to 16 children,
which requires conditional use approval

SITE & ZONE DESCRIPTION

This home is in the Oquirrh Meadows Subdivision and the surrounding area is predomininately zoned R-1-6 and
R-1-8.
          Request: Conditional Use                                                  File #: CUP2023-000792




ISSUES OF CONCERN/PROPOSED MITIGATION

No issues of concern are identified at this time. All agency reviewers have given approval to the conceptual review
with additional information and revisions being required for technical review and final approval. Compliance with
the requirements of the overpressure area (which are primarily building design elements) will be ensured as part
of the technical review process.


PLANNING STAFF ANALYSIS

Parking

Home daycares are required to have one parking spot as well as one additional parking spot for every additional
employee that is working there. The applicant has adequate parking space from their garage and driveway to
accommodate one parking spot.



Landscaping




Conditional Use Summary                                                                                 Page 2 of 3
          Request: Conditional Use                                                 File #: CUP2023-000792

Landscaping is not required for home day cares. The backyard is designated as a play area and there is a vinyl
fence around the yard.

Signage

The applicant has not proposed any signage as part of their application.

Conditional Use

Home day cares are conditional uses based on the number of students per 19.04.293.A of the Magna Code.

Review Criteria

The Planning Commission is the decision making body for conditional use permits. If approval is granted for this
conditional use then the projet will advance into the technical review phase which will then review the project
based on compliance with the code.

MSD staff has reviewed the application and has found that the proposal with staff recommendations is consistent
with the surrounding land uses. Full compliance with required ordinances and policies will be verified through the
subsequent technical review process before the issuance of the Land Use permit, and license inspection process.
Staff finds that the application meets, or will meet with conditions, all required standards of the ordinance
necessary for preliminary approval by the Planning Commission.

PLANNING STAFF RECOMMENDATION

Based on the findings stated above, the MSD Planning Staff recommends that the Magna Planning
Commission grant approval for the conditional use for a home day care with the following conditions:

    1.    The applicant be required to comply with the requirements of the R-1-6 zone and Chapter 19.04.293.
    2.    The applicant be required to comply with the off-street parking requirements.
    3.    The applicant be required to comply with the requirements of the sign code.
    4.    The applicant be required to comply with the requirements from all reviewing agencies.

                                            Files # CUP2022-000730

                                      Conditional Use Summary

Public Body: Magna Planning Commission
Meeting Date: February 9, 2023
Parcel ID: 14-33-227-069-0000
Current Zone: C-2
Property Address: 7341 W 3500 S
Request: Conditional Use for an apartment building (multi-family dwelling)
Applicant Name: Tia Crow
MSD Planner: Justin Smith
MSD Planning Staff Recommendation: Planning Commission Approval


PROJECT SUMMARY

The applicant, Tia Crow, is applying for a conditional use for an apartment building. The building will consist of
17 units. The apartment building would be 3 stories tall and have two garage parking stalls and 32 uncovered
stalls.

SITE & ZONE DESCRIPTION

This property is located along 3500 S and is located just west of the 3500 S and 7200 S intersection. The lot is
currently vacant with the exception of a small paved portion of driveway in the northeast corner that provides
access to the auto parts store and a Verizon cell tower in the southwest portion of the lot.




ISSUES OF CONCERN/PROPOSED MITIGATION

No issues of concern are identified at this time, with the exception of Engineering. Engineering is requesting a
geotechnical report that meets Salt Lake County Standards.


PLANNING STAFF ANALYSIS
          Request: Conditional Use                                                 File #: CUP2022-000730

The applicant is proposing an apartment building.

Parking

This apartment building will have 17 apartment units and 2 parking spaces are required per dwelling unit. That
would require 34 parking spaces, the exact number that have been provided including the garage spots. If
Planning Commission feels that it is necessary additional guest parking may be required.

Landscaping

The applicant’s landscape plan meets MSD requirements. There are trees and shrubbery along the frontage and
trees and shrubbyery along the eastern and southern portion of the lots. The dumpster will have a masonry
enclosure.

Signage

The applicant has not proposed any signage on the lot.

Conditional Use

Apartment buildings are allowed in the C-2 zone as a conditional use in the C-2 zone as multiple dwellings. There
are some additional lot size requirements for residential uses in the C-2 zone. The minimum required lot tisze is
5,000 square feet per building with an additional 750 square feet per unit in that building. With 17 units inone
building that would require around 17,000 square feet or about 0.39 acres. The lot is 0.72 acres in size. The lot
is roughly 125 feet wide and and the C-2 zone requires residential lots to be 50 feet across. The required
setbacks are 8 feet to the side, 25 feet to the front, and 30 feet to the rear. The building is 30 feet from the
road, but 20 feet from the property line. The first 10 feet have been dedicated to the Magna Metro Township,
but this change has not been made on our maps.

Review Criteria

The Planning Commission is the decision making body for conditional use permits. If approval is granted for this
conditional use then the projet will advance into the technical review phase which will then review the project
based on compliance with the code.

MSD staff has reviewed the application and has found that the proposal with staff recommendations is consistent
with the surrounding land uses. Full compliance with required ordinances and policies will be verified through the
subsequent technical review process before the issuance of the Land Use permit, and license inspection process.
Staff finds that the application meets, or will meet with conditions, all required standards of the ordinance
necessary for preliminary approval by the Planning Commission.

PLANNING STAFF RECOMMENDATION

Based on the findings stated above, the MSD Planning Staff recommends that the Magna Planning
Commission grant approval for the conditional use for multi-family dwelling with the following conditions:

    1.    The applicant be required to comply with the requirements of the C-2 zone.
    2.    The applicant be required to comply with the landscaping requirements.
    3.    The applicant be required to comply with the off-street parking requirements.
    4.    The applicant be required to comply with the requirements of the sign code.



Conditional Use Summary                                                                                Page 2 of 3
        Request: Conditional Use                                               File #: CUP2022-000730

   5. The applicant be required to provide a geotechnical report to Salt Lake County Engineering’s
      standards.
   6. The applicant be required to comply with the requirements from all reviewing agencies.

                                            Files # SUB2022-000747

                                      Preliminary Plat Summary

Public Body: Magna Planning Commission
Meeting Date: March 9, 2023
Parcel ID: 14-21-126-004-0000
Current Zone: M-2
Property Address: 7823 W 2100 S
Request: Kersey Creek Subdivsion
Applicant Name: Michael Hartvigsen
MSD Planner: Justin Smith
MSD Planning Staff Recommendation: Planning Commission Approval


PROJECT SUMMARY

The applicant, Michael Hartvigsen, is proposing a 4 lot commercial subdivision in Magna named Kersey Creek.
The subdivision is 10.02 acres in size and will have two one-acre lots, one 1.468 acre lot, and a 5.663 acre lot.
Access is provided by a 54 foot wide private drive that runs the length of the first three lots and touches the
fourth. Lot 3 has received Planning Commission approval for electrical office and storage.

SITE & ZONE DESCRIPTION

This property is located along the south side of 2100 S just west of American Eagle Ready-Mix. The lot is flat and
does not have any elevation or topographical challenges that would make it hard or impossible to develop on
the lots.
        Request: Subdivision                                                         File #: SUB2022-000747




ISSUES OF CONCERN/PROPOSED MITIGATION

The only issue of concern at the time is that Salt Lake County Engineering would like a note stating that all future
developments on this subdivision will require a Traffic Impact Study. All other agency reviewers have given an
“ok” to the conceptual review with additional information and revisions being required for technical review and
final approval. Compliance with the requirements of the inland port overlay district will be ensured as part of the
site development review process.



SubdivisionSummary                                                                                       Page 2 of 3
         Request: Subdivision                                                       File #: SUB2022-000747

PLANNING STAFF ANALYSIS

Lot 3 of this subdivision has received conditional use approval from the Planning Commission and is currently in
the technical review process.

Access

The private access provides access to access to all 4 lots and has adequate width to accommodate traffic going
both ways.

Blocks

The “block” that is included in this subdivision meets our code requirements by being less than 1,600 feet in
length and by having an access wide enough to accommodate two tiers of lots. Blocks intended for business and
industrial use must be large enough to have adequate space for parking and deliveries. None of the lots are
unusually small and they should all be adequate in size to support a business or industrial use.

Lots

The lots are all shaped like a box and do not interfere with the topography of the area. All of the lots meet the
minimum size requirements of the M-2 zone.

Review Criteria

The Magna Metro Township Code highlights the Planning Commission as the final land use authority for
subdivisions in the Magna Metro Township.

MSD staff has reviewed the application and has found that the proposal with staff recommendations is consistent
with the surrounding land uses. Full compliance with required ordinances and policies will be verified through the
subsequent technical review process before the issuance of the Land Use permit, and license inspection process.
Staff finds that the application meets, or will meet with conditions, all required standards of the ordinance
necessary for preliminary approval by the Planning Commission.

PLANNING STAFF RECOMMENDATION

Based on the findings stated above, the MSD Planning Staff recommends that the Magna Planning
Commission grant approval for the Preliminary Plat with the following conditions:

    1.   The applicant be required to comply with the requirements of the M-2 zone.
    2.   The applicant be required to comply with the subdivision code.
    3.   The applicant be required to pay any fees or post bond to guarantee any improvements.
    4.   The applicant be required to provide a lighting plan that satisfies all requirements of MSD staff.
    5.   The applicant be required to comply with the requirements from all reviewing agencies.
    6.   The final plat shall state that all development within the subdivision is subject to compliance with
         Chapter 16.01 Inland Port Overlay District.

ATTACHMENTS:
   A. Preliminary Plat
   B. Conceptual Comments 2.28.23
